content.title: Rory McIlroy Masters Round 1 scorecard and leaderboard update
content.text: Updated April 9, 2026, 9:48 p.m. ETFollow along with live updates of all the first-round action at the Masters Tournament.There's a new and improved version of Rory McIlroy at the Masters in 2026. The outdated one, missing that elusive green jacket, is now gone. He is replaced by a more relaxed McIlroy ambling through Augusta with the vigor of a defending champion.Thursday marks the official start of the Northern Irish golfer's defense. And he will indeed be a calmer golfer, no longer straining to put together four rounds but allowing himself to enjoy the endeavor.“I feel so much more relaxed," McIlroy said on Wednesday. "I know that I'm going to be coming back here for a lot of years, going to enjoy the perks that the champions get here."Among those perks has to be knowing every crack and crevice at an event he will now have played at 18 times. There is a reason he is among the favorites to be atop the leaderboard come Sunday.USA TODAY Sports will have updates through the first round as Rory McIlroy searches for back-to-back green jackets at the Masters: Masters leaderboard 2026You can get the latest leaderboard updates here.T1. Rory McIlroy -5 (F)T1. Sam Burns: -5 (F)T3. Jason Day -3 (F)T3. Kurt Kitayama -3 (F)T3. Patrick Reed -3 (F) Rory McIlroy Round 1 Masters scoreMcIlroy finished with a 5-under par and heads to the clubhouse in a tie for the lead. He made 11 pars, six birdies and only one bogey. Rory McIlroy on No. 18 holeMcIlroy's final tee shot of Round 1 failed to reach the fairway. Go figure. Instead it went directly into the bunker, but he had a nice lie and struck his second shot to the middle of the green. And he nearly made birdie, sending his putt to within a few feet of the hole before tapping in for par. McIlroy heads to the clubhouse 5-under and in a tie for first place with Sam Burns. Rory McIlroy on No. 17 holeMcIlroy nearly took sole possession of the lead on 17, but was a little too strong on his birdie putt on the 17th hole. His drive off the tee went 332 yards on the left side of the fairway. McIlroy attacked the hole with his second shot, hitting to the back of the green and just 11 feet from the hole. His putt for birdie cruised past the hole, but he netted another par to head to the final hole in a tie for first. Rory McIlroy on No. 16 holeMcIlroy's streak of birdies ended, but a par will do just fine. He made the green on his first shot of the par-3 hole and rolled his next putt to just 2 feet from the hole. He tapped in for the par to maintain a share of the lead. Rory McIlroy on No. 15 holeAfter a 349-yard blast just off the left of the fairway, McIlroy left his second shot in a perfect spot before the water. His third shot went over the drink and within 30 feet of the hole. And then what did McIlroy do? He drained the putt to give him a share of the lead. McIlroy held his fist up as fans roared. Rory McIlroy on No. 14 holeHere comes Rory! A spectacular drive right down the middle of the fairway was followed by a stunning shot to within 7 feet of the hole. McIlroy then knocked down his birdie putt, his second consecutive birdie, to give him a score of 4-under par. He's in second place, all by himself, just one shot behind Sam Burns. Rory McIlroy on No. 13 holeMcIlroy's tee shot on 13 could have spelled doom, as he put his ball into the trees. But he punched out to the middle of the fairway, knocked to 14 feet of the pin and made a birdie putt to give himself 3-under par and just two shots off the lead. Rory McIlroy on No. 12 holeMcIlroy got some help from nature on No. 12, where his tee shot hit some trees to the left of the fairway and bounced back into play. He capitalized on his good fortune by hitting his second shot to within 3 feet and then making another par putt. Rory McIlroy on No. 11 holeMcIlroy has found his stride off the tee, hitting his drive right down the middle. It set him up nicely for a second shot that he took to within 30 feet of the hole. He left his birdie putt left of the hole by 3 feet before making his seventh par of the day. Rory McIlroy on No. 10 holeThat's two consecutive fairways for McIlroy, who hit his second shot to the fringe of the green and left his third shot just short of the hole before tapping in for par. Rory McIlroy on No. 9 holeMcIlroy hits the turn on a roll. After four consecutive pars, he has made two straight birdies and heads to No. 10 at 2-under par. He also snapped his skid of missing fairways, driving his tee shot right down the middle. He parked his second shot to within 8 feet of the hole and made his birdie putt. Rory McIlroy on No. 8 holeThe par streak is over, but the missed fairways streak stays intact. Though he missed the fairway with his drive, McIlroy was lined up perfectly to strike his second shot onto the green, just 24 feet from the hole. His try for eagle was short, but McIlroy made his birdie putt to get to 1 under for the round. Rory McIlroy on No. 7 holeMcIlroy's drive on No. 7 sent patrons running as he sliced it right of the fairway. He's now 0 for 5 on fairways. After his second shot went off the back of the green, he chipped his third shot to within 3 feet of the putt and knocked down his fourth consecutive par. Rory McIlroy on No. 6 holeMcIlroy sailed his first shot just over the green on the par-3 sixth hole, but it was still in good enough shape to set him up for his third consecutive par. McIlroy remains at even after six holes. Rory McIlroy on No. 5 holeAnother hole, another missed fairway, but McIlroy continues to save himself with his irons. His second shot rolled back to 50 feet from the hole, and he putted his next shot to 5 feet. He made his second consecutive par, and third in five holes. Rory McIlroy on No. 4 holeOn the par-3 No. 4, McIlroy's first shot went 173 yards and within 40 feet of the hole. He gave too much power on his ensuing putt, which also went right of the hole to about 6 feet. McIlroy, however, saved par to stay even. Rory McIlroy on No. 3 holeAdrenaline must be at an all-time high for McIlroy, who muscled his drive 336 yards over the left-side bunkers and off the fairway once again. He chipped his second shot onto the green, less than 50 feet away from the hole, but ended up three-putting to make bogey. Rory McIlroy on No. 2 holeMcIlroy is now 0 for 2 on hitting the fairway, but 2 for 2 in avoiding disaster. His drive on the par-5 No. 2 hole went over a bunker and into a woodsy area. Despite a clear lie and look for his second shot, but he pulled it left of the green and into the gallery. But his third shot was a perfect chip to within 3 feet of the cup. He knocked in the putt for birdie. Rory McIlroy on No. 1 holeMcIlroy started his Masters title defense by making par on the first hole. His drive went left of the fairway, just in front of some patrons. His second shot was a clear one, which he knocked to the fringe of the green. He chipped from there to within 5 feet of the hole and then made his putt for par.Rory McIlroy tee time: Golfer start time, pairingsMcIlory will have a bit of a wait to tee off on Thursday. Here is his start time and his group.10:31 a.m. ET – Rory McIlroy, Cameron Young, Mason Howell (a)Where to watch the Masters: TV Channel, streaming ThursdayAll main feed coverage for all four days can also be found on Masters.com and the Masters App. Here's a breakdown of the main broadcast schedule for the 2026 Masters:Prime Video: 1-3 p.m. ETESPN/ESPN App: 3-7:30 p.m. ETWatch the 2026 Masters from Augusta with FuboMasters Tournament 2026: How to watch, TV channel, live streamPrime Video makes its debut as a Masters broadcaster this year and will carry the event for the first time ever with two hours of streaming coverage for the first and second rounds. ESPN will provide linear cable coverage for those two days, picking up where Amazon Prime leaves off.On the weekend, CBS will again handle the main feed for the Masters. The first two hours of coverage on Saturday and Sunday will air exclusively on Paramount+, before the network takes over for the remainder of each round.All main feed coverage for all four days can also be found on Masters.com and the Masters App. Here's a breakdown of the main broadcast schedule for the 2026 Masters:Watch The Masters on Prime VideoAll times Eastern.Thursday and Friday (April 9-10)Prime Video: 1-3 p.m.ESPN/ESPN App: 3-7:30 p.m.Saturday and Sunday (April 11-12)Paramount+: Noon-2 p.m.CBS/Paramount+: 2-7 p.m. 2026 Masters odds: Favorites at AugustaAll odds via BetMGM on Wednesday, April 8.Favorites1. Xander Schauffele (+1400) Masters predictions: Sleeper picks at AugustaUSA TODAY Sports' Jon Hoefling offers up a trio of sleepers plus one intriguing longshot who have the talent to buck the odds and put on a green jacket if things break their way.Tommy Fleetwood (+2200)Fleetwood is someone who often gets glossed over when discussing the best golfers in the world, but he's been consistently good at Augusta the last eight years, finishing in the top-25 in five of those tournaments, including a tie for third place in 2024. He tends to play up at Augusta and is fresh off winning the Tour Championship in 2025.Patrick Reed (+3300)Patrick Reed won the Masters back in 2018, so he knows what it takes to get the green jacket. Of course, his presence on the LIV Tour for the last few years certainly hasn't helped his chances. He might be a little too used to playing in three-day tournaments at this point. However, Reed is different.In the seven Masters Tournaments since his victory, he's finished top-12 or better in five of them, and that includes a top-ten finish in three of his last five Masters appearances. A bet on Reed to finish in the top-20 could pay out massively.Jordan Spieth (+3300)It's been just over 10 years since Spieth won the green jacket at Augusta, and he's been inconsistent ever since. Five years ago, he tied for third. Four years ago, he missed the cut. Three years ago, he tied for fourth. Two years ago, he missed the cut. Last year, he tied for 14th.Sure, the pattern would indicate that he's due for some regression in 2026, but streaks are meant to be broken and Spieth has played in this tournament enough to warrant some confidence that he can still do well. After all, he's finished top-25 in more than half of the events he's played this year.
